features.text: Patient is a 32-year-old female.
Experiencing IBS flare-ups with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.
Abdominal pain is cramping and sharp, located in the lower belly, and comes and goes.
Nausea occurs more frequently after eating out, especially after spicy or fatty foods.
Vomiting occurs occasionally, but not too often.
Symptoms have worsened since starting to eat out more often on weekends.
Had prior IBS flare-ups, especially around August 2019.
Previous IBS flare-up triggers included eating out, spicy or fatty foods, and drinking alcohol on weekends.
No other gastrointestinal conditions or allergies reported.
No family history of gastrointestinal disorders.
No recent stool tests, blood tests, or imaging studies for current symptoms.
Currently using Bentyl and Zofran as needed for symptoms.
Not consistently taking Citrucel fiber supplement.
No recent changes in medication regimen.
No weight loss, rectal bleeding, or persistent fever during flare-up.
Bowel habits have changed, with two to three bowel movements per day, mostly formed stools, but more diarrhea after eating out or drinking.
Abdominal pain occurs frequently after eating out or drinking alcohol, especially after spicy or fatty foods.
Fried chicken does not seem to trigger symptoms as much.
No recent changes in diet or alcohol consumption, but increased frequency of eating out on weekends.
Symptoms worsen after eating out, especially with spicy or fatty foods or alcohol consumption, typically in the evening.
No blood or mucus in stools, and stool consistency is mostly formed.
Increased frequency of bowel movements, usually two to three times a day.
Patient is trying to avoid triggers by watching diet and alcohol intake.
